_note: One control arm for composition_motif_adopt, added 2026-08-24 alongside the declaration composition_motif_adopt.motif_id <- composition_motif_search.

scenarios.prompt: Adopt motif "A Grudge Older Than the Holder" — copy that built-in trope into my library so I can customise it.
scenarios.prompt_source:
meta.synonyms['adopt motif'] VERBATIM AND CONTIGUOUS, with the target named around it.

🔴 THE CONTIGUITY IS NOT STYLE, IT DECIDES WHETHER THE TOOL IS ON THE WIRE AT ALL. Checked against the deployed matcher before this scenario was written:
    'Adopt motif "A Grudge Older Than the Holder" — copy that built-in trope ...' -> ANSWERABLE
    'Adopt the built-in motif "A Grudge Older Than the Holder" ...'                -> NOT
Inserting two words INSIDE the declared synonym drops the tool from the answerable set, so a more specific prompt can be a strictly worse one. The motif named is a real system row (code wuxia.inherited_feud), one of the 84 the seed_assert counts.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM motif WHERE status='active' AND owner_user_id IS NULL
seed_assert.why:
EIGHTY-FOUR system/unlisted motifs already exist, so there is genuinely something to adopt and the model must FIND one — composition_motif_book_list / a motif search is the supplier. Read from the store rather than assumed. NOTE the deliberate asymmetry with batch 15's arc templates: the system arc-template library is EMPTY, so this is the first tool in the loop whose cross-tenancy source actually has rows.

🔴 status='active' ADDED 2026-08-23 by the lifecycle-predicate gate. The tool reads active rows only (get_by_codes filters status='active'), so without this the assertion could pass over rows the tool is structurally unable to see — which is exactly what happened to composition_motif_link_edit for fifteen runs. Verified NOT to change the seeded value: all 84 system motifs are active today, so this tightens the assertion without moving its number.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM motif WHERE owner_user_id='019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c' AND code LIKE 'adopted-%'
seed_assert.why: SCOPED, not a headcount of the caller's library. That library is 152 and MOVING — the other scenarios in this batch seed into it, and my own seed-smoke added a row while I was verifying the fixture. The system side (84, owner_user_id NULL) is stable and is asserted above; here the check is simply that no ADOPTED clone exists yet, so one appearing is attributable to this turn.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a clone lands with NO confirm card (Tier W — its own description says adopting 'crosses the tenancy boundary and counts against your library quota', which is why it is human-confirmed), OR the model invents a motif_id rather than listing the built-ins first, OR it passes retag_genres the author never mentioned — retagging is optional and silently re-genre-ing an adopted motif changes what it will match later.

ship_audit.gate: The card IS the audit — this is a cross-tenancy copy against a quota.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a motif_id that is neither public nor the caller's must be refused.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — 🔴 THIS TOOL CROSSES THE BOUNDARY BY DESIGN, so the check is the inverse of every other one in this batch: adopting a PUBLIC motif must be allowed, and adopting another USER's private motif must not.

scenarios._rerun_note: Re-run at --concurrency 1. The batch-19 arms lost 21/25 then 14/25 runs to the provider's 'upstream sent error with no error message'. Concurrency 4 -> 2 took it 84% -> 56%, so pressure is part of it but not all of it; a one-turn smoke at concurrency 1 was clean. A transport failure is not a model result, so the earlier arms are VOID rather than evidence of 0/5.
scenarios._control_note:
CONTROL ARM. It does NOT replace composition-motif-adopt and does not retire its finding.

THE ORIGINAL MEASURES SOMETHING REAL AND THE MODEL PASSES IT: its measured turn is a bare confirmation, 'Yes, go ahead and do it.', after a turn that listed the built-ins. The model answers 'you haven't told me WHICH motif' on 5 of 5 — correct, because 'one of the built-in tropes' names no target among 84. That arm keeps its result.

WHAT IT CANNOT MEASURE is the tool, for a reason the matcher makes plain: the answerable set for 'Yes, go ahead and do it.' is EMPTY, so the tool was never advertised in the turn under test — surfaced 0/5 is not a selection finding, it is a turn with no vocabulary in it. Whether an intent should reach back to the previous user message is P16-PROSE-CONFIRMATION and an owner's question.

So this arm asks the answerable version of the same request, exactly as composition-generate-named-chapter sits beside composition-generate. If the tool is still not called here, the supplier declaration was not the blocker and that is the finding.
